correctness.rationale: Monomial integration gives exact independent gamma energies and beta-binomial CDF with block composition multiplicities. Uniform Chernoff and method-of-types bounds yield the logarithmic CDF exponent within \(O(\log m)\), including the upper-tail index. Fixed-degree multiplicity expansion plus a bounded-variation weighted Riemann sum proves the explicit order-\(m^d\) rate and \(O(m^{d-1}\log m)\) remainder. Standard-library exact and finite convergence tests independently exercise the formulas, not the proof of the limit.

evidence: Charles–Estienne (arxiv:1803.03149), their spectral-window Weyl law and trace theorem, use regular endpoint-vanishing test functions: a singular logarithm is outside the stated trace assumptions.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Regular functional calculus results do not bound the deep exponentially small part of the spectrum whose total log cost has order \(m^d\). A more general determinantal LDP might imply the leading logarithmic exponent implicitly; its relationship to the explicitly evaluated two-block rate is a residual priority risk, not an asserted absence.

Existing inspected explicit spherical results are restricted to complex dimension one, while the claimed log-determinant rate weights beta-binomial tails by multivariate composition multiplicities.

value.rationale: The spectral determinant measures simultaneous mass retention for every holomorphic mode in a finite projective/Fock quantization sector, and is equivalently a natural determinantal gap probability. Exact exponential rates distinguish higher-dimensional coordinate splits and thresholds; the explicit relative-entropy integral and uniform order \(m^{d-1}\log m\) bound are quantitative structural information not provided by eigenvalue diagonalization alone.
